segments.name: Oil and Gas
segments.description: Explores and produces crude oil and natural gas from blocks in Argentina, including the Vaca Muerta formation.
segments.evidence: We are engaged in the oil and gas business through the exploration and exploitation of direct interests in blocks located in Argentina, with operations in 9 production blocks, 2 exploratory blocks and 470 productive wells.

segments.name: Generation
segments.evidence: Our generation installed capacity reached 5,472 MW as of December 31, 2025, representing approximately 12% of Argentina's installed capacity.

segments.name: Petrochemicals
segments.description: Produces petrochemical products at two Argentine plants for domestic customers.
segments.evidence: We are engaged in the petrochemicals business through two plants located in Argentina which produce styrene, styrene butadiene rubber and polystyrene, with a domestic market share of 86% and 98% (per Company estimates), respectively, as of December 31, 2025.

segments.name: Holding and Other Business
segments.description: Holds interests in gas transportation, high-voltage electricity transmission, oil pipelines and related energy infrastructure companies.
segments.evidence: Our holding and other business segment recorded U.S.$ 24 million in revenue and an operating profit of U.S.$ 68 million for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.

revenueModel.text: Pampa earns revenue from selling crude oil, natural gas, electricity and petrochemical products, largely collected in Argentine Pesos.
revenueModel.evidence: Although a significant portion of our revenue in the spot market for power generation is denominated in U.S. Dollars, our revenues are mainly collected in Argentine Pesos at an exchange rate that is fixed at the end of each month.

changes.text: In 2016, Pampa acquired Petrobras Participaciones S.L. and subsequently merged Petrobras Argentina and other subsidiaries into Pampa.
changes.evidence: In July 2016, we acquired from Petrobras all of the shares of Petrobras Participaciones S.L., which in turn owned, at such time, 67.2% of the shares of Petrobras Argentina (the "Acquisition").
